arguments.content:
Intro: A Maltese's long, silky coat needs gentle, regular care to stay glossy, matt-free, and tangle-free — the process from bath to blow-dry is straightforward once you have the right products and tools.

1) Gather the correct products and tools (10–15 minutes)
- What to get: a gentle, pH-balanced dog shampoo (hypoallergenic or oatmeal-based for sensitive skin), a conditioning/rinse-out conditioner formulated for long coats, a leave-in detangling spray or conditioning mist, a tearless puppy/face shampoo or gentle saline wipes for the eyes, and a silicone coat serum or finishing spray for shine and flyaways.
- Recommended examples (optional): Earthbath Oatmeal & Aloe, TropiClean Hypoallergenic, Isle of Dogs Silky Coating Conditioner, Chris Christensen White on White (for whitening/brightening), and a good quality leave-in detangler. Avoid human shampoos and heavy oils.
- Tools: slicker brush, pin brush, stainless steel comb (wide-toothed and fine-toothed), dematting tool (for small mats only), grooming scissors and thinning shears (safety rounded tips), microfiber towels, a high-absorbency towel or chamois, a low-heat dog dryer or a human dryer with a cool/low setting and diffuser, grooming clips or bands for topknots, non-slip mat for the tub, and optional grooming table with arm.

2) Pre-bath brushing and quick health check (5–15 minutes)
- Thoroughly brush through the coat to remove loose hair and gentle tangles. Start with a slicker brush, follow with a pin brush, and finish with a comb to check for hidden mats close to the skin.
- Check ears, eyes, skin (redness, sores), and paws. Trim nails if needed before the bath — it’s easier when the dog is dry and calmer, but a quick check reduces surprises.

3) Prepare the bath area and water temperature (5 minutes)
- Use lukewarm water (about 90–100°F / 32–38°C). Put a non-slip mat in the tub and have all products and towels within reach.
- Protect the eyes and ears: don’t pour water directly over the head; use a cup or sprayer and/or cover the ear openings gently with cotton if your dog tolerates it (remove afterward).

4) Wet, lather, and shampoo gently (5–7 minutes)
- Thoroughly wet the coat, then apply a small amount of dog shampoo, working from neck to tail. Lather gently and avoid vigorous scrubbing — long coats tangle more with rough handling. Use a tearless shampoo or mild warm water + soft cloth to clean the face.
- Rinse thoroughly; residue causes tangles and irritation. Expect several rinses until water runs clear.

5) Apply conditioner and detangle in the bath (2–5 minutes)
- Apply a moisturizing, rinse-out conditioner from mid-length to ends (avoid heavy application on the roots/scalp unless the product is lightweight). Leave it in for the time the product recommends (often 1–3 minutes).
- Use a wide-tooth comb in the bath to gently work the conditioner through the hair, taking out remaining small tangles — conditioner helps loosen them so you avoid matting later.

6) Final rinse and gentle squeeze-dry (3–5 minutes)
- Rinse completely with lukewarm water. Squeeze excess water gently (don’t wring). Use a microfiber towel or chamois to blot and absorb moisture — Maltese coats hold water and dry more quickly when blotted.

7) Towel and partial air-dry, then apply leave-in products (5–10 minutes)
- Once mostly towel-dried, apply a lightweight leave-in detangler or conditioning spray to the mid- and end-lengths. Spray lightly and comb through with a wide-tooth comb to distribute product and prevent tangles during blow-drying.

8) Blow-dry on low heat while brushing (15–35 minutes)
- Use a low-heat setting and a gentle airflow (or a dog-specific dryer). Keep the nozzle moving and aim slightly against hair growth to help the coat lift and straighten.
- While drying, use a slicker brush to hold sections and a pin brush or comb to finish each section. Work in small sections from neck to tail, keeping the coat untangled as it dries. For a full-length show coat this is the longest step — expect 20–45 minutes; for a shorter pet trim 15–25 minutes.

9) Final brush, trim, and tidy (10–20 minutes)
- Once dry, use the comb to check for any remaining tangles or tiny mats; remove gently with fingers or a dematting tool for very small spots. Trim hair around the eyes, feet, sanitary areas and any split ends with grooming scissors as needed.
- Apply a tiny amount of silicone serum or finishing spray to the ends to reduce static and keep the coat smooth — use sparingly to avoid weighing the coat down.

10) Aftercare schedule and maintenance tips (5–10 minutes per short session)
- Expect total time: generally 45–90 minutes from start to finish for a cooperative Maltese (shorter for trimmed pet cuts, longer for full-length show preparation).
- Daily: gentle brushing or combing for 5–10 minutes to prevent tangles.
- Weekly: a more thorough 15–30 minute brushing session and spot checks for mats.
- Bath frequency: every 3–4 weeks for most pet Maltese; sooner if your dog gets particularly dirty or if recommended by your vet. Over-bathing strips natural oils, so use conditioning products and leave-in detanglers to maintain moisture.
- If you find recurring mats near ears, armpits, or behind legs, address them promptly with conditioner and careful combing; for large mats consult a professional groomer rather than forcing removal.

Conclusion: With the right gentle shampoos, conditioners, and regular brushing, a Maltese coat stays soft, shiny, and matt-free — consistent short maintenance sessions prevent long, stressful grooming days. If mats or skin issues persist, consult a professional groomer or your veterinarian.
